subject: Hosted API: transient egress shaping — account impact and status page notice
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@oceanicbio.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Status] Hosted API — transient egress shaping affecting responses

Hi Samira,

I wanted to let you know we are investigating elevated 5xx rates and increased p95 latency from the hosted API impacting requests for Oceanic Bio (account ID: OB-4721). We observed the first spike at ~10:05 PDT with generation/chat endpoints returning 502/504 and stalled streaming responses.

Immediate actions weve taken:
- Opened incident INC-20270520-201 and posted a short advisory to the status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20270520-201
- Enabled automatic cross-region fallback (us-west -> us-east) for affected traffic to reduce errors for sessions that support region fallback
- Captured runtime and network egress logs (attached: ops-incident-log-20270520.txt) for our post-incident analysis

Preliminary signal shows a sudden spike in egress throughput from a small set of hosts in our us-west cluster; cloud provider telemetry indicates a transient egress shaping event that coincided with the spike. We are actively confirming whether requests were retried/returned errors for any persisted state in your workflow.

We will provide a follow-up within 2 hours with a timeline and remediation plan. If you have a specific example request ID or timestamp showing an error, please reply and well prioritize it.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your integration and are treating it as high priority.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:35:10 -0700
Subject: Internal: immediate RCA notes and mitigation actions (INC-20270520-201)

Team — quick notes while the incident is active: 

What we see so far:
- Spike in egress bytes from 10:04-10:12 PDT originating from 6 inference nodes in us-west-1. Cloud provider flagged egress shaping on the node's subnet for sustained high throughput to a small external CIDR block.
- Our smart-routing policy had conservative thresholds for region fallback; by the time fallback kicked in ~10:07 the affected flows had accumulated retries and some streaming sessions aborted.
- No signs of data corruption or payload truncation; client-side stack traces indicate timeouts/connection resets.

Immediate mitigation (done):
- Enabled aggressive fallback to us-east for the OB-4721 routing policy (completed 10:09)
- Increased client-side keepalive timeouts at the gateway to reduce premature connection closures
- Opened JIRA INF-3421 to track config changes and postmortem tasks

Next steps (owner):
- Markus: collect kernel/open-socket metrics from the six nodes & coordinate with cloud provider to confirm egress shaping root cause (owner: markus.klein)
- Aditya: prepare a short runbook for rolling fallback threshold changes and test on canary (owner: aditya.rao)
- Lauren: draft customer-facing summary and credit proposal (owner: lauren.bishop)
- Hannah: assemble postmortem and timeline (owner: hannah.schmitt)

Please escalate if additional nodes are affected. Ill post another update when we have confirmation from the provider.

Cc: Oceanic Bio Platform Team <platform@oceanicbio.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 12:28:00 -0700
Subject: Incident resolved — summary and follow-up (INC-20270520-201)

Hi Samira,

Thank you for your patience. Were marking INC-20270520-201 as resolved at 12:20 PDT. Summary and follow-up below.

What happened (brief):
- At ~10:04 PDT a subset of nodes in our us-west inference pool experienced unexpected egress shaping from the cloud provider which caused connection resets and elevated 502/504 responses for some customers, including Oceanic Bio.

Actions we took:
- Enabled cross-region fallback earlier in the routing policy to divert traffic to us-east (reduced errors by ~90% within 8 minutes)
- Worked with the cloud provider to remove the egress shaping flag on affected subnets (completed 11:05 PDT)
- Captured detailed logs and stack traces; no evidence of data loss or truncated payloads for ingress requests — streaming sessions that aborted were due to connection resets and retries.

Customer impact and timeline for Oceanic Bio:
- Window of impact: 10:04 - 10:12 PDT (primary) with residual elevated retries until ~10:20 while fallback warmed
- Observed failure rate on your traffic: ~18% for a short window (matches your report)
- Request ob-prod-7812: traced — error was a connection reset during streaming; payload rows were not persisted by our runtime. We can assist in re-playing that job if useful.

Remediation and next steps:
- We will ship a config change to make fallback thresholds more aggressive for accounts that opt-in (INF-3421).
- We are updating our health-run monitoring to detect cloud egress shaping signals earlier to trigger automatic rerouting.
- Postmortem and remediation doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=postmortem_INC-20270520-201 (draft).
- Action item: Lauren will reach out separately on a good-faith credit for this disruption.

Again, sincerely sorry for the interruption. If youd like a short call to walk through the timeline and any compensatory steps, Im available this afternoon.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
